why: Your site has a real page for homes, one for businesses, a blog, and a phone number one tap away. So this isn't a rescue. It's what a full build adds, from our audit.

Your headlines are slogans. The homepage says “From Dim to Dazzling – We've Got the Wiring Right.” The residential page says “Powering Homes, One Wire at a Time!” The contact page has no headline at all.
On a phone, every page is laid out 768 pixels wide inside a 390-pixel screen, so it scrolls sideways. And 58 of the 61 images on your homepage have no alt text.

Two of your Google reviews describe a tech treating a parent's house with care. The review block on your site showed no text when we checked. The demo opens with electrician in Wichita, KS, gives outlet repair and EV charger installation a page each, and puts your customers' words on the page.

Your reviews written onto the page.

confirm.heading: What we'd confirm with you
confirm.intro: Google and AI tools see different answers about your business in different places. We wrote this demo from your reviews and your site. On a short onboarding call, we'd confirm these so everything says the same thing.
items: Your site says “Since 2005,” while a Wichita State alumni list says the company was founded in 1988, so which year should every listing use?
Your site and directories list (316) 262-1440, while two BBB listings show 316-771-0064 and 316-308-4488, so which number should every listing use, and are the others still yours?
Your site and directories list 408 S Ida, while another listing shows 225 S Ida St #102, so which address should every listing use?
Your demo has an EV charger page that rests on one review, and Kathy S. mentions electrical trenching in another, so do you offer both?

lead.heading: Why we led with the electrician you can send to your mom's house
lead.text: We led with the mom's-house call because two customers wrote about their mothers' homes, and nobody else on the web has those reviews. Add 408 S Ida and your weekday hours, and Google has a reason to show you for a search a generic electrician page can't answer.

unverified.heading: What we couldn't verify, and why it matters
unverified.intro: We marked these on the demo as yellow "to confirm" tags instead of guessing, because we won't put a claim on your site we can't back up. Your pages and the listings online don't agree on a few of them, and others have no answer at all.

items.why: Your site says "Since 2005" and another listing says 1988, and a son or daughter handing a parent's house to a stranger wants a number that holds up.
"Greater Wichita area" doesn't tell someone across town whether you'll come to their mom's street.
Your site doesn't mention one, and a person who can't be at the house will ask what happens if the fix doesn't hold.

unverified.closing: This is what our onboarding call nails down. Fifteen minutes, and every tag becomes a real, true line.
